conceptTag: Just in time vs just in case
readerTitle: Why the inventor of just in time kept a stockpile
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Toyota, 2011년 지진과 2021년 반도체 부족) + 가상 적용 (철물 유통업체, 사내 IT팀)
insight: 재고를 줄일지 쌓을지는 회사 전체의 방침이 아니라 품목마다 정하는 선택이다. 다시 채우기 어렵고 떨어지면 비싼 품목에만 여유분을 둔다.
misconception: 재고는 무조건 낭비이므로 최대한 줄여야 한다. 반대로, 위기를 한 번 겪으면 모든 것을 넉넉히 쌓아 두는 것이 안전하다.

sources.text: Reuters (2021). How Toyota thrives when the chips are down. 2011년 이후 반도체 등 핵심 부품 비축에 관한 보도
Toyota 공급망 관련 공개 자료 (2011년 동일본 대지진 이후 공급업체 정보 데이터베이스 구축)
철물 유통업체, 사내 IT팀 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 2011년 지진 때 Renesas 공장 피해로 Toyota 생산이 영향을 받은 점, 이후 Toyota가 하위 공급업체까지 파악하는 데이터베이스를 만든 점을 게시 전 1차 자료로 확인하세요.
Reuters(2021년 3월) 보도: Toyota가 공급업체에 반도체 등 핵심 부품의 여유 재고를 요청했고, 덕분에 반도체 부족 초기에 경쟁사보다 생산을 오래 유지했다는 내용. 비축 기간(보도상 수개월)은 정확한 수치를 쓰지 않고 "a few months"로만 표현했습니다.
Toyota가 2021년 하반기 반도체 부족 장기화로 감산한 사실(2021년 9월 발표)을 확인하세요. 카드에는 감산 비율을 쓰지 않았습니다.
철물 유통업체의 리드타임(펌프 12주, 나사 2일)과 사내 IT팀의 노트북 대기 6주는 설명용 가상 수치입니다.

cards.title: Why the inventor of just in time kept a stockpile
body: Toyota made lean inventory famous. Parts arrive just before they're needed, and almost nothing sits on a shelf.
Yet when a global chip shortage hit carmakers in 2021, Toyota reportedly kept building cars longer than many rivals. The reason: a stockpile it had quietly built years earlier.

image.label: A lean factory line next to one well-stocked shelf
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 텅 빈 선반이 이어진 깔끔한 자동차 조립 라인 옆에, 작은 칩 상자가 가득 찬 선반 하나만 눈에 띄게 놓여 있음. 실제 자동차 브랜드 로고나 차량 디자인은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Where should the extra stock go?
body: You run a hardware distributor that supplies 40 local stores. You keep stock lean, and it has kept costs low.

Screws and tape come from several suppliers and arrive in two days. One popular water pump comes from a single overseas factory and takes 12 weeks. When stores run out of pumps, customers go elsewhere. What do you change?

options.text: Nothing. Lean stock has worked, so keep ordering everything as it sells
options.feedback: You keep costs low, but a 12-week wait on a single supplier means one hiccup empties every store of pumps for months.

options.text: Double the stock of everything, just to be safe
options.feedback: You'll rarely run out, but you tie up cash and space in screws you could restock in two days.

options.text: Hold extra pumps and keep fast-restock items lean
options.feedback: You pay to store only what is slow and hard to replace. That's the idea in this lesson.

cards.title: An earthquake showed where the system was thin.
body: In 2011, a huge earthquake struck Japan. Among the damaged factories was one belonging to a major chip maker that supplied Toyota and others. Car production stalled.

Toyota found it didn't fully know which suppliers stood behind its own suppliers. Afterwards, it mapped them and reportedly asked suppliers to hold **extra stock of hard-to-replace parts**, such as chips, enough for a few months.
Most parts stayed lean. Only the fragile ones got a cushion.

cards.title: Just in time vs just in case
body: **Just in time** means getting stock only as you need it. You save cash, space and waste, but any delay stops you quickly.
**Just in case** means holding extra stock as a cushion against delays or demand spikes. You keep running when things go wrong, but you pay to store goods that may sit idle.
Neither is right on its own. The skill is choosing which items get which treatment.

image.label: A dial between 'Just in time' and 'Just in case'
image.brief: 가로 다이얼 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 끝 "Just in time"(얇은 선반, 아이콘: 동전 절약), 오른쪽 끝 "Just in case"(가득 찬 선반, 아이콘: 방패). 여러 상자 아이콘이 다이얼의 서로 다른 위치에 놓여 있음.

cards.title: Three questions for each item.
body: Ask these about any item you depend on:
list: **How long to restock?** Two days can run lean. Twelve weeks needs a cushion.
**How many sources?** Many suppliers can cover for each other. One supplier can't.
**What does running out cost, compared with holding it?** A cheap part that stops a whole line is worth stocking. A pricey item with easy substitutes is not.
cards.callout: Lean where restocking is easy. Cushioned where it's slow, single-source or costly to miss.
cards.softwareNote: Reserving server capacity in advance is just in case. Scaling up on demand is just in time. Many teams reserve a steady base and buy the peaks as they come.

cards.title: Every business already mixes the two.
body: A good restaurant buys fish daily, just in time, because it spoils. It buys salt, napkins and rice in bulk, just in case, because they keep and cost little to store.
A shop stocks up before the holidays, when running out costs the most, and runs lean in quiet months.
The question isn't which camp you belong to. It's where on the dial each item, and each season, should sit.

cards.title: Cushions cost money, and they run out too.
body: Extra stock ties up cash and space. It can spoil or go out of date. It can also hide problems, like a slow supplier, that lean stock would have exposed.
And a cushion only buys time. As the chip shortage dragged on, Toyota also had to cut production later in 2021.
After a crisis, the urge is to stockpile everything. That trades one risk for a steady drain on cash.

cards.title: Now it's an IT team inside a company.
body: You run IT at a 2,000-person company. You order laptops only when a hire signs, to avoid idle equipment. Lately, the standard laptop takes six weeks to arrive, and new hires sit with nothing to work on.
Designers need a special model, but only a few join each year. What do you do?

options.text: Keep a small stock of the standard laptop, and order designer models as needed
options.feedback: You cushion the item that's common and slow to arrive, and stay lean on the rare one. A few idle laptops cost less than weeks of idle new hires.

options.text: Keep a stock of both models to be safe
options.feedback: No one waits, but expensive designer laptops may sit for months and go out of date before anyone uses them.

options.text: Stay fully lean and ask managers to give more notice before hires start
options.feedback: No spare laptops to pay for, but you're betting every hiring plan arrives six weeks early. One late signing leaves someone idle.

cards.title: Run lean by default. Cushion what's slow, single-source or costly to miss.
body: Just in time and just in case aren't opposing beliefs. They're settings you choose item by item.
**Try it today:** list the five items your business can't run without. For each, write how long it takes to restock and how many places you can get it. Which one needs a cushion?
